στόμα.long: the mouth, speech, eloquence in speech, the point of a sword.
στόμα.sd: the mouth (as if a gash in the face); by implication, language (and its relations); figuratively, an opening (in the earth); specially, the front or edge (of a weapon)
στόμα.der: probably strengthened from a presumed derivative of the base of G5114 (τομώτερος);
στόμα.as:
στόμα, -τος, τό
[in LXX chiefly for פֶּה ;]
the mouth: of man, Mt 15:11, Jo 19:29, Ac 11:8, al.; of animals, Mt 17:27, II Ti 4:17 (fig.), He 11:33, Ja 3:3, al.; fig., of inanimate things (ποταμοῦ, Hom.), ἤνοιξεν ἡ γῆ τὸ σ., Re 12:16; σ. μαχαίρας (Heb. פִּי־חֶרֶב, Ge 34:26 al.), the edge of the sword, Lk 21:24, He 11:34; esp. of the mouth as the organ of speech: opp. to καρδία, Mt 12:34, Ro 10:8, 10; in various phrases (some cl., some resembling Hebrew; cf. Bl., § 40, 9): ἀνοίγειν τ. σ. (v.s. ἀνοίγω); σ. πρὸς σ. (פֶּהאֵל־פֶּה, Nu 12:8; = cl., κατὰ σ., Hdt., al.), face to face, II Jo 12, III Jo 14; διὰ τοῦ σ. (of the Holy Spirit), Lk 1:70, Ac 1:16, al.; ἀπὸ (ἐκ) τοῦ σ. (cf. ἀπὸ σ. εἰπεῖν, Plat., al.), of speaking by word of mouth, Lk 22:71, Ac 22:14; δόλος (ψεῦδος) ἐν τ. σ., I Pe 2:22, Re 14:5(LXX); metaph., ἡ ῥομφαία τοῦ σ., Re 2:16. By meton., for speech (Soph.): Mt 18:16(LXX), Lk 19:2221:15, II Co 13:1

στρέφω.long: I turn, am converted, change, change my direction.
στρέφω.sd: to twist, i.e. turn quite around or reverse (literally or figuratively)
στρέφω.kj: convert, turn (again, back again, self, self about)
στρέφω.der: strengthened from the base of G5157 (τροπή);
στρέφω.as:
στρέφω
[in LXX chiefly for הפך, also for סבב, etc. ;]
to turn: c. acc. rei dat. pers., Mt 5:39; = ἀποσ-, to bring back, Mt 27:3 (cf. Is 38:8); reflexively (WM, § 38, 1), to turn oneself, Ac 7:42; c. acc. seq. εἰς, = μετασ-, to change, Re 11:6. Pass., reflexive, to turn oneself: seq. εἰς, Jo 20:14, Ac 7:3913:46; ptcp., στραφείς, c. indic., Mt 7:69:2216:23, Lk 7:99:5514:2522:61, Jo 1:3820:16; id. seq. πρός, Lk 7:4410:22 (WH, R, om.), ib. 2323:28; metaph., to change: absol., Mt 18:3, Jo 12:40 (cf. ἀνα-, ἀπο-, δια-, ἐκ, ἐπι-, κατα-, μετα-, συ(ν)-, ὑπο-στρέφω).†

στενός.der: probably from the base of G2476 (ἵστημι);
στενός.as:
στενός, -ή, -όν
[in LXX for צַר, etc. ;]
narrow: fig (v MM, xxiii), Mt 7:13, 14, Lk 13:24.†

σταφυλή.sd: a cluster of grapes (as if intertwined)
σταφυλή.der: probably from the base of G4735 (στέφανος);
σταφυλή.as:
σταφυλή, -ῆς, ἡ
[in LXX for עֵנָב ;]
a bunch of grapes: Mt 7:16, Lk 6:44, Re 14:18. "σ. is properly the ripe grape-cluster as opp. to ὄμφαξ, cf. Ge 40:10, Jb 15:33; as contrasted with βότρυς, it describes the grapes rather than the cluster on which they grow" (Swete, Apoc., 187 f.).†

στέγη.g: a flat roof of a house
στέγη.long: a flat roof of a house.
στέγη.der: strengthened from a primary (a "thatch" or "deck" of a building);
στέγη.as:
στέγη, -ης, ἡ
(< στέγω) [in LXX: Ge 8:13 (מִכְסֶה), etc. ;]
a roof: Mk 2:4; of entering a house, εἰσέρχεσθαι ὑπὸ τὴν σ., Mt 8:8, Lk 7:6 (cf. MM, xxiii).†

στρατιώτης.sd: a camper-out, i.e. a (common) warrior (literally or figuratively)
στρατιώτης.der: from a presumed derivative of the same as G4756 (στρατιά);
στρατιώτης.as:
στρατιώτης, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX; II Ki 23:8 B1, II Mac 5:1214:39, III Mac 3:12 ; IV Mac3 * ;]
a soldier: Mt 8:9, Mk 15:16, Jo 19:2, Ac 10:7, al.; metaph., σ. Χριστοῦ Ἰησ., II Ti 2:3.†

στρουθίον.as:
στρουθίον, -ου, τό
[in LXX chiefly for צִפּוֹר ;]
dimin. of στρουθός
a sparrow: Mt 10:29, 31, Lk 12:6, 7.†

σταυρός.sd: a stake or post (as set upright), i.e. (specially), a pole or cross (as an instrument of capital punishment); figuratively, exposure to death, i.e. self-denial; by implication, the atonement of Christ
σταυρός.as:
* σταυρός, -οῦ, ὁ
1. an upright pale or stake (Hom., Hdt., Thuc., al.)
2. In late writers (Diod., Plut., al.) of the Roman instrument of crucifixion, the Cross: of the Cross on which Christ suffered, Mt 27:32, 40, 42, Mk 15:21, 30, 32, Lk 23:26, Jo 19:17, 19, 25, 31, Col 2:14, He 12:2; θάνατος σταυροῦ, Phl 2:8; τ. αἷμα τοῦ σ., Col 1:20. Metaph., in proverbial sayings: αἴρειν (λαμβάνειν, βαστάζειν) τὸν σ., Mt 10:3816:24, Mk 8:3410:21, 15:21, Lk 9:2314:27 (for an interesting ex. of metaph. use in π., v. MM, xxiii) By meton., for Christ's death on the Cross: I Co 1:17, Ga 5:116:12, 14, Eph 2:16, Phl 3:18; ὁ λόγος ὁ τοῦ σ., I Co 1:18.†

στάχυς.sd: a head of grain (as standing out from the stalk)
στάχυς.as:
στάχυς, -υος, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for שִׁבֹּלֶת ;]
an ear of corn: Mt 12:1, Mk 2:234:28, Lk 6:1.†

στάδιος.long: (a) a stadium, one eighth of a Roman mile, (b) a race-course for public games.
στάδιος.sd: a stade or certain measure of distance; by implication, a stadium or race-course
στάδιος.der: from the base of G2476 (ἵστημι) (as fixed);
στάδιος.as:
στάδιον, -ου, τό pl., στάδια (Jo 6:19, T), and metapl., στάδιοι (v. B1., § 9, 1),
[in LXX: Da LXX 4:9, Su 37, II Mac 11:512:9 ff. * ;]
a stadium, i.e.
1. a measure of length = 600 Greek feet or 1⁄8 of a Roman mile Mt 14:24 (Rec., WH, txt., R, mg.), Lk 24:13, Jo 6:1911:18, Re 14:2021:16, and, this being the length of the Olympic course,
2. a race-course: I Co 9:24.†

στυγνάζω.long: I am gloomy, have a somber countenance, am shocked.
στυγνάζω.sd: to render gloomy, i.e. (by implication) glower (be overcast with clouds, or sombreness of speech)
στυγνάζω.as:
† στυγνάζω
(< στυγνός, sombre, gloomy, sullen, Is 5:17, Wi 17:5, Da LXX 2:12*), [in LXX: Ez 27:3528:1932:10 (שָׁמֵם)* ;]
to have a sombre, gloomy appearance: of the human countenance (RV, his countenance fell), Mk 10:22; of the sky (so στυγνότης, Polyb., iv, 21, 1), Mt 16:3 (|[WH]|, R, mg., om.).†

στατήρ.long: an Attic silver coin equal in value to the Jewish shekel.
στατήρ.sd: a stander (standard of value), i.e. (specially), a stater or certain coin
στατήρ.as:
στατήρ, -ῆρος, ὁ
[in Aq., Sm., for שֶׁקֶל ;]
a stater;
(a) a weight;
(b) a coin (used by late writers of the Greek τετράδραχμον): Mt 17:2726:16, WH, mg.†

σταυρόω.long: I fix to the cross, crucify; fig: I destroy, mortify.
σταυρόω.sd: to impale on the cross; figuratively, to extinguish (subdue) passion or selfishness
σταυρόω.as:
σταυρόω, -ῶ
(< σταυρός), [in LXX: Es 7:9 (תּלה), Es 8:13 * ;]
1.to fence with pales, impalisade (Thuc.).
2. In late writers (Polyb., FlJ; but ἀνασταυρόω is more common) to crucify: c. acc. pers., Mt 20:1923:3426:227:22 ff. 28:5, Mk 15:16 ff. 16:6, Lk 23:21, 23, 3324:7, 20, Jo 19:6 ff., Ac 2:364:10, I Co 1:13, 232:2, 8, II Co 13:4, Ga 3:1, Re 11:8; metaph., Ga 5:246:14.†

στρώννυμι.sd: to "strew," i.e. spread (as a carpet or couch)
στρώννυμι.der: prolongation from a still simpler , (used only as an alternate in certain tenses) (probably akin to G4731 (στερεός) through the idea of positing);
στρώννυμι.as:
στρωννύω or στρώννυμι
(v. Bl., § 23, 1; Veitch, s.v.), [in LXX for יצע hoph., etc. ;]
to spread: ἱμάτια ἐν τ. ὁδῷ (εἰς τ. ὁδόν), Mt 21:8, Mk 11:8; of making a bed, στρῶσον (sc. τ. κλίνην) σεαυτῷ, Ac 9:34; of furnishing a room, ἐστρωμένον, spread with carpets or carpeted couches (cf. Ez 23:41), Mk 14:15, Lk 22:12.†

στράτευμα.sd: an armament, i.e. (by implication) a body of troops (more or less extensive or systematic)
στράτευμα.as:
** στράτευμα, -τος, τό
(< στρατεύω), [in LXX: I Mac 9:34, II Mac 5:248:2112:3813:13; pl., Jth 11:8, IV Mac 5:1 * ;]
1. = στρατεία (Hdt., al.).
2.an army, a host: pl., Mt 22:7, Re 9:1619:14, 19; = soldiers, company of soldiers, Ac 23:10, 27; pl., Lk 23:11.†

στέφανος.sd: a chaplet (as a badge of royalty, a prize in the public games or a symbol of honor generally; but more conspicuous and elaborate than the simple fillet, G1238 (διάδημα)), literally or figuratively
στέφανος.der: from an apparently primary (to twine or wreathe);
στέφανος.as:
στέφανος, -ου, ὁ
(< στέφω, to encircle), [in LXX chiefly for עֲטָרָה ;]
1.that which surrounds or encompasses (as a wall, a crowd: Hom., al.).
2.a crown, i.e. the wreath, garland or chaplet given as a prize for victory, as a festal ornament, or as a public honour for disting­uished service or personal worth (so to sovereigns, especially on the occasion of a παρουσία, q.v.; cf. Deiss., LAE, 372 ff.; on its use in LXX for the golden crown of royalty (prop., διάδημα, q.v., cf. Hort and Mayor on Ja 1:12): Mt 27:29, Mk 15:17, Jo 19:2, 5, I Co 9:25, Re 4:4, 106:29:712:114:14. Metaph.: Phl 4:1, Re 3:11; τ. δικαιοσύνης (cf. Deiss., LAE, 312), II Ti 4:8; τ. δόξης, I Pe 5:4; καυχήσεως, I Th 2:19 (v. M, Th., in l.); τ. ζωῆς (gen. appos.), Ja 1:12, Re 2:10.†

στήκω.long: I stand fast, stand firm, persevere.
στήκω.sd: to be stationary, i.e. (figuratively) to persevere
στήκω.der: from the perfect tense of G2476 (ἵστημι);
στήκω.as:
† στήκω late Pres., formed from perf., ἕστηκα (v. B1., § 17; WH, App., 169; Kennedy, Sources, 158; M, Pr., 238; MM, xxiii),
[in LXX: Ex 14:13 A, Jg 16:26 B, III Ki 8:11 B * ;]
= ἵστημι, to stand: Mk 3:3111:25, Jo 1:26, Re 12:4 (ἕστηκεν T). Metaph., to stand firm, stand fast: absol., Ga 5:1 (but v. Field, Notes, 189 f.), II Th 2:15; seq. ἐν, Jo 8:44 (ἕστηκεν, T, R, mg.), I Co 16:13, Phl 1:274:1; c. dat., Ro 14:4.†

στενάζω.long: I groan, expressing grief, anger, or desire.
στενάζω.sd: to make (intransitively, be) in straits, i.e. (by implication) to sigh, murmur, pray inaudibly
στενάζω.as:
στενάζω
[in LXX for אנח ni., אנק, etc. ;]
to groan ("the word denotes feeling which is internal and unexpressed," Mayor, Ja., 162): Mk 7:34, II Co 5:2, 4, He 13:17, Ja 5:9 (EV, murmur); ἐν ἑαυτοῖς, Ro 8:23 (cf. ἀνα-, συ(ν)-στενάζω).†
SYN.: v.s. κλαίω

στίλβω.long: I shine, glisten, flash, am radiant.
στίλβω.as:
στίλβω
[in LXX: Na 3:3 (לַהַב), etc. ;]
to shine, glisten: Mk 9:3.†

στιβάς.as:
** στιβάς, -άδος, ἡ,
[in Aq.: Ez 46:23 (טִירוֺת) * ;]
a litter of leaves or rushes: pl., Mk 11:8 (Rec. στοιβ-).†

στολή.long: a long robe, worn by the upper classes in the East.
στολή.sd: equipment, i.e. (specially), a "stole" or long-fitting gown (as a mark of dignity)
στολή.as:
στολή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< στέλλω), [in LXX chiefly for בֶּגֶד, also for לְבֻשׁ, etc. ;]
1.an equipment, an armament (Æsch.).
2. Equipment in clothes, apparel, esp. flowing raiment, a festal robe: (cf. Jh 3:6, Es 8:15, I Mac 6:15): Mk 12:3816:5, Lk 15:2220:46, Re 6:117:9, 13, 1422:14.†

στασιαστής.der: from a compound of G4862 (σύν) and a derivative of G4714 (στάσις);
στασιαστής.as:
*† στασιαστής
(< στασιάζω, to stir up sedition, Jth 7:15, II Mac 4:3014:6 *)
= Att.. στασιώτης,
a rebel, revolutionist, one who stirs up sedition: Mk 15:7 (FlJ, al.).†

στάσις.long: an insurrection, dissension; originally: standing, position, place.
στάσις.sd: a standing (properly, the act), i.e. (by analogy) position (existence); by implication, a popular uprising; figuratively, controversy
στάσις.as:
στάσις, -εως, ἡ
(< ἵστημι), [in LXX chiefly for עמד, its parts and derivatives, also for רִיב (Pr 17:14), etc. (v. Deiss., BS, 158 f.) ;]
1.a standing, place, status: σ. ἔχειν (Polyb., v, 5, 3; and cf. Lat. locum habere), He 9:8.
2.insurrection, sedition: Mk 15:7, Lk 23:19, 25, Ac 19:4024:5.
3. In poets and late prose, strife, dissension (cf. MM, xxiii) Ac 15:223:7, 10.†

στεῖρα.der: a contraction from G4731 (στερεός) (as stiff and unnatural);
στεῖρα.as:
στεῖρος, -ον also -α, -ον,
[in LXX for עֲקֶרֶת, עֲקָרָה ;]
barren: of a woman, Lk 1:7, 3623:29, Ga 4:27(LXX).†

στρατιά.long: an army; met: a host of angels, the hosts of heaven (i.e. the stars).
στρατιά.sd: from the base of G4766 (στρώννυμι), as encamped); camp-likeness, i.e. an army, i.e. (figuratively) the angels, the celestial luminaries
στρατιά.der: feminine of a derivative of (an army;
στρατιά.as:
στρατιά, -ᾶς, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for צָבָא ;]
1. = στρατός, an army, a host: of angels (III Ki 22:19, al.), Lk 2:13; of the stars of heaven (Je 8:2, II Ch 33:3), Ac 7:42.
2. As sometimes in cl. (poët.), = στρατεία: II Co 10:4, T (WH, RV, στρατεία).†

στρατεύομαι.long: I wage war, fight, serve as a soldier; fig: of the warring lusts against the soul.
στρατεύομαι.sd: to serve in a military campaign; figuratively, to execute the apostolate (with its arduous duties and functions), to contend with carnal inclinations
στρατεύομαι.der: middle voice from the base of G4756 (στρατιά);
στρατεύομαι.as:
στρατεύω and depon., -ομαι, so always in NT
(< στρατός, an encamped army), [in LXX for מההּ hith., יצא, צבא; metaph., IV Mac 9:23 ;]
used of the general, to make war, do battle, and (chiefly) of the soldiers serving under him, to serve as a soldier: Lk 3:14, I Co 9:7, II Ti 2:4. Metaph. (cf. MM, ii, xxiii), of spiritual conflict, to war, make war: II Co 10:3, I Ti 1:18, Ja 4:1, I Pe 2:11.†

στιγμή.g: a point of time, an instant
στιγμή.long: a moment, point of time, an instant.
στιγμή.sd: a point of time, i.e. an instant
στιγμή.as:
στιγμή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< στίζω, to prick), [in LXX: Is 29:5 (פֶּתַע), II Mac 9:11 * ;]
a prick, a point; metaph., σ. χρόνου, a moment: Lk 4:5.†

στηρίζω.long: (a) I fix firmly, direct myself towards, (b) generally met: I buttress, prop, support; I strengthen, establish.
στηρίζω.sd: to set fast, i.e. (literally) to turn resolutely in a certain direction, or (figuratively) to confirm
στηρίζω.der: from a presumed derivative of G2476 (ἵστημι) (like G4731 (στερεός));
στηρίζω.as:
στηρίζω
[in LXX for סמך, שׂוּם (שׂים), etc. ;]
to fix, set fast, make fast: Lk 16:26; τ. πρόσωτον (Ez 6:213:17, al.; v. Dalman, Words, 30 f.), Lk 9:51. Metaph., to confirm, establish: c., acc., Lk 22:32, Ac 18:23, Ro 1:1116:25, I Th 3:2, 13, II Th 3:3, Ja 5:8, I Pe 5:10, Re 3:2; id. seq. ἐν, II Th 2:17, II Pe 1:12.†

στῆθος.as:
στῆθος, -ους, τό
[in LXX: Ex 28:23, 26 (29, 30) (לֵב), etc. ;]
the breast: Jo 13:2521:10, Re 15:6; as a sign of penitence, τύπτειν (εἰς) τὸ σ., Lk 18:1323:48,†

στρατόπεδον.sd: a camping-ground, i.e. (by implication) a body of troops
στρατόπεδον.der: from the base of G4756 (στρατιά) and the same as G3977 (πεδινός);
στρατόπεδον.as:
στρατό-πεδον, -ου, τό
(στρατός + πέδον, a plain), [in LXX: Je 41 (34):1 (חַיִל), II Mac 8:12, al. ;]
(a)a military camp;
(b)an army: Lk 21:20.†

στρατηγός.g: a general, magistrate, captain of the temple
στρατηγός.long: (a) a general or leader of the army, (b) a magistrate or governor, (c) captain of the temple.
στρατηγός.sd: a general, i.e. (by implication or analogy) a (military) governor (prætor), the chief (præfect) of the (Levitical) temple-wardens
στρατηγός.der: from the base of G4756 (στρατιά) and G71 (ἄγω) or G2233 (ἡγέομαι);
στρατηγός.as:
στρατηγός, -οῦ, ὁ
(< στρατός, ἄγω), [in LXX chiefly for סָגָן (always in pl.), שַׂר ;]
1. a military commander, a general (Hdt., al.).
2. A civic commander, a governor, magistrate (Hdt., Xen., al.): Ac 16:20, 22, 35, 36, 38.
3. The commander of the Levitical guard of the Temple, ὁ σ. τ. ἱεροῦ (EV, captain of the Temple): Ac 4:15:24, 26; pl., Lk 22:4, 52.†
SYN.: ἄρχων (cf. EGT on Ac 16:20; Ramsay, St. Paul, 217).

στοά.as:
στοά, -ᾶς, ἡ
[in LXX: Ez 40:18 (רִצְפָּה), etc. ;]
a portico: Jo 5:2; used of the covered colonnade in the Temple (EV, porch), Jo 10:23, Ac 3:115:12 †

στερεόω.sd: to solidify, i.e. confirm (literally or figuratively)
στερεόω.as:
στερεόω, -ῶ
(< στερεός), [in LXX: Is 42:5 (רקע), Je 5:3 (חזק pi.), etc. ;]
(a)to make firm or solid;
(b)to strengthen, make strong; c. acc. pers., Ac 3:16; τ. βάσεις, pass., ib. 7. Metaph. (cf. Je, l.c.): τ. πίστει, pass., Ac 16:5.†

Στοά.as:
στοά, -ᾶς, ἡ
[in LXX: Ez 40:18 (רִצְפָּה), etc. ;]
a portico: Jo 5:2; used of the covered colonnade in the Temple (EV, porch), Jo 10:23, Ac 3:115:12 †

Στέφανος.long: Stephen, one of the seven original deacons at Jerusalem, and the first martyr.
Στέφανος.as:
Στέφανος, -ου, ὁ
Stephen: Ac 6:5, 8, 97:598:211:1922:20.†

στεναγμός.as:
στεναγμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(< στενάζω), [in LXX for אֲנָחָה, אֲנָקָה, נְאָקָה, etc. ;]
a groaning: Ac 7:34 (LXX κραυγή), Ro 8:26.†

στέμμα.as:
* στέμμα, -τος, τό
(< στέφω, to put around, enwreath)
a wreath, garland: as used in sacrifices, Ac 14:13.†

στοιχέω.sd: to march in (military) rank (keep step), i.e. (figuratively) to conform to virtue and piety
στοιχέω.der: from a derivative of (to range in regular line);
στοιχέω.as:
στοιχέω, -ῶ
(< στοῖχος, a row), [in LXX: Ec 11:6 (כָּשֵׁר) * ;]
to be in rows (of waves, plants, etc., as well as of men), to walk in line (esp. of marching in file to battle; Xen., Cyr., vi, 3, 34, al.). Metaph., in late writers, to walk by rule: Ac 21:24; c. dat., to walk by or in (as a rule of life), Ro 4:12 (cf. MM, xxiii), Ga 5:256:16, Phl 3:16 (cf. συν-στοιχέω).†

στενοχωρία.long: a narrow space, great distress, anguish.
στενοχωρία.der: from a compound of G4728 (στενός) and G5561 (χώρα);
στενοχωρία.as:
στενοχωρία, -ας, ἡ (v. supr.)
[in LXX for צוּקָה, etc. ;]
narrowness of space, want of room (Thuc., al.). Metaph. (Xen., Polyb., De 28:53, Wi 5:3, al.), difficulty, distress: θλίψις καὶ (ἢ) σ., Ro 2:98:35 (EV, anguish); pl. (cf. Bl., § 32, 6; WM, 220), II Co 6:412:10.†
SYN.: θλίψις, q.v

Στάχυς.long: Stachys, a Christian man at Rome.
Στάχυς.as:
Στάχυς, -υος, ὁ
Stachys: Ro 16:9 (v. Lft., Phl., 174; MM, xxiii).†

Στεφανᾶς.as:
Στεφανᾶς, -ᾶ, ὁ
Stephanas: I Co 1:1616:15, 17.†

στέγω.long: I cover, conceal, ward off, bear with, endure patiently.
στέγω.sd: to roof over, i.e. (figuratively) to cover with silence (endure patiently)
στέγω.as:
** στέγω
(cf. Lat. tego), [in LXX: Si 8:17 * ;]
1. prop., to cover closely, to protect by covering, esp. to keep water in or out (Soph., Plat., al.).
2.to cover, keep secret, conceal (Si, l.c., Polyb., al.): I Co 13:7, R, mg.
3. By covering to ward of, bear up under, endure (for exx., v., Lft., Notes, 40; M, Th., 36): I Co 9:1213:7, I Th 3:1, 5.†

στάδιον.g: one eighth of a Roman mile
στάδιον.long: (a) a stadium, one eighth of a Roman mile, (b) a race-course for public games.
στάδιον.sd: a stade or certain measure of distance; by implication, a stadium or race-course
στάδιον.der: from the base of G2476 (ἵστημι) (as fixed);
στάδιον.as:
στάδιον, -ου, τό pl., στάδια (Jo 6:19, T), and metapl., στάδιοι (v. B1., § 9, 1),
[in LXX: Da LXX 4:9, Su 37, II Mac 11:512:9 ff. * ;]
a stadium, i.e.
1. a measure of length = 600 Greek feet or 1⁄8 of a Roman mile Mt 14:24 (Rec., WH, txt., R, mg.), Lk 24:13, Jo 6:1911:18, Re 14:2021:16, and, this being the length of the Olympic course,
2. a race-course: I Co 9:24.†

στενοχωρέομαι.long: (I keep some one in a tight place), I press upon, cramp, restrain.
στενοχωρέομαι.sd: to hem in closely, i.e. (figuratively) cramp
στενοχωρέομαι.as:
στενο-χωρέω, -ῶ
(< στενός + χῶρος, space) [in LXX: Jos 17:15 (אוּץ), Jg 16:16 (אלץ pi.), Is 28:19 (20) (קצר) Is 49:19 (צרר), IV Mac 11:11 * ;]
1.to be straitened (cf. Is 49:19); metaph., to be anxious (Hipp., al.).
2. In late writers, trans., to straiten, compress (LXX, Diod., al.; π. ap. MM, xxiii): pass., trop., II Co 4:86:12.†

στέλλομαι.g: I arrange, take care, withdraw from
στέλλομαι.long: I set, arrange; mid: I provide for, take care, withdraw from, hold aloof, avoid.
στέλλομαι.sd: properly, to set fast ("stall"), i.e. (figuratively) to repress (reflexively, abstain from associating with)
στέλλομαι.der: probably strengthened from the base of G2476 (ἵστημι);
στέλλομαι.as:
στέλλω
[in LXX (mid.): Ma 2:5 (חתת ni.), Pr 31:24 (26), Wi 7:1414:1, II Mac 5:1, III Mac 1:194:11 * ;]
1. prop., to set, place, arrange, fit out; hence, mid., to set oneself for, prepare (Wi, II Mac, ll. c.).
2.to bring together, gather up (in Hom. of furling sails), hence to restrain, check; mid., to restrain or withdraw oneself, hold aloof, avoid: II Co 8:20; seq. ἀπό, II Th 3:6
(cf. ἀπο-, ἐξ-απο-, συν-απο-, δια-, ἐπι-, κατα-, συ(ν)-, ὑπο-στέλλω).†

στρατεία.long: warfare, military service; of Christian warfare.
στρατεία.sd: military service, i.e. (figuratively) the apostolic career (as one of hardship and danger)
στρατεία.as:
στρατεία (on the orthogr., v. Deiss., BS, 181 f.), -ας, ἡ
(< στρατεύω), [in LXX chiefly for צָבָא ;]
an expedition, a campaign, warfare: metaph., II Co 10:4 (-τιά, T), I Ti 1:18.†

στῦλος.sd: properly akin to the base of G2476 (ἵστημι)); a post ("style"), i.e. (figuratively) support
στῦλος.as:
στύλος (T, στῦλος, as in cl.), -ου, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for עַמּוּד, also for קֶרֶשׁ, etc. ;]
a pillar, regarded especially as a support: σ. πυρός, Re 10:1; σ. ἐν τ. ναῷ, fig., Re 3:12, Metaph., Ga 2:9; τ. ἀληθείας, I Ti 3:15.†

στοιχεῖον.long: (a) plur: the heavenly bodies, (b) a rudiment, an element, a rudimentary principle, an elementary rule.
στοιχεῖον.sd: something orderly in arrangement, i.e. (by implication) a serial (basal, fundamental, initial) constituent (literally), proposition (figuratively)
στοιχεῖον.der: neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of G4748 (στοιχέω);
στοιχεῖον.as:
** στοιχεῖον, -ου, τό
[in LXX: Wi 7:1719:18, IV Mac 12:13 * ;]
prop., one of a row (στοῖχος) or series, hence,
1.the shadow-line of a dial (Aristoph.).
2.an elementary sound or letter of the alphabet (Anth., Plut., π.).
3.the elements or rudiments of knowledge (Arist., al.) He 5:12; πτωχὰ σ., Ga 4:9; σ. τοῦ κόσμου, ib. 3, Col 2:8, 20 (but v. infr.).
4. The material elements of the universe (Plat.; LXX, ll. c.): II Pe 3:10, 12.
5. The heavenly bodies (Diog. Laert.).
6. The demons or tutelary spirits of nature (Enoch., Test., Sol., al.; for this sense in Ga, Col, ll. c., v. ICC on Col 2:8; Enc. Bibl., s.v. " Elements ").†

στίγμα.sd: a mark incised or punched (for recognition of ownership), i.e. (figuratively) scar of service
στίγμα.as:
στίγμα, -τος, τό
(< στίζω, to prick), [in LXX: Ca 1:11 (נְקֻדָּה) * ;]
a tattoed mark or brand: τὰ σ. τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, Ga 6:17 (v. Lft., in l.; Deiss., BS, 349; LAE, 303; MM, xxiii).†

στερέωμα.as:
στερέωμα, -τος, τό
(< στερεόω), [in LXX: Ge 1:6 ff., Ps 18 (19):1150:1, Ez 1:22-2610:113:5, Da LXX, TH 3:(56), 12:3 (רָקִיעַ), De 33:26 (שׁחק), Ps 17 (18):270 (71):3 (סֶלַע), Es 9:29, I Es 8:78 (82), Si 43:1, 8, I Mac 9:14 * ;]
a solid body;
(a)a support, foundation (Arist., al.); metaph., strength (Ps 1770, I Mac, ll. c.); steadfastness, firmness: τ. πίστεως, Col 2:5;
(b) the dome of heaven (believed to be a solid canopy), the firmament (LXX).†

στόμαχος.as:
* στόμαχος, -ου, ὁ
(< στόμα),
prop., a mouth, an opening;
(a) in early Gk. writers, the throat;
(b) of the opening of the stomach (Arist.);
(c) in later writers (Plut., al.), the stomach: I Ti 5:23.†

στρατολογέω.long: I collect an army, enlist troops.
στρατολογέω.sd: to gather (or select) as a warrior, i.e. enlist in the army
στρατολογέω.der: from a compound of the base of G4756 (στρατιά) and G3004 (λέγω) (in its original sense);
στρατολογέω.as:
*† στρατολογέω, -ῶ
(< στρατός, λέγω),
to levy a troop, enlist soldiers: II Ti 2:4 (Diod., Plut., al.).†

στεφανόω.sd: to adorn with an honorary wreath (literally or figuratively)
στεφανόω.as:
στεφανόω, -ῶ
(< στέφανος), [in LXX for עטר ;]
c. acc. pers.,
to crown: of a victor, II Ti 2:5. Metaph., δόξῃ κ. τιμῇ, He 2:7, 9 (LXX).†

στερεός.sd: stiff, i.e. solid, stable (literally or figuratively)
στερεός.as:
στερεός, -ά, -όν
[in LXX: Nu 8:4 (מִקְשָׁה); σ. πέτρα, Is 5:28 (צַר), etc. ;]
hard, firm, solid: τροψή, He 5:12, 14; θεμέλιος, fig., II Ti 2:19. Metaph.,
(a) in bad sense, hard, cruel (Hom., al.);
(b) in good sense, steadfast, firm: τ. πίστει, I Pe 5:9.†

στυγητός.der: from a derivative of an obsolete apparently primary (to hate);

στάμνος.der: from the base of G2476 (ἵστημι) (as stationary);
στάμνος.as:
στάμνος, -ου (ὁ and), ἡ
[in LXX: Ex 16:33 (צִנְצֶנֶת), III Ki 12:2414:3 (בַּקְבֻּק), Da LXX Bel 32 * ;]
prop., an earthen jar for racking off wine, hence, generally, a jar: He 9:4.†

στρεβλόω.long: I twist, torture; met: I twist or pervert language.
στρεβλόω.sd: to wrench, i.e. (specially), to torture (by the rack), but only figuratively, to pervert
στρεβλόω.as:
στρεβλόω, -ῶ
(< στρέφω), [in LXX: II Ki 22:27 (פּתל hithp.), III Mac 4:14, IV Mac 9:1712:4, 1115:14 * ;]
to twist, torture. Metaph. (cf. II Ki, l.c.), to twist or pervert language: II Pe 3:16.†

στηριγμός.as:
** στηριγμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(< στηρίζω), [in Sm.: Is 3:1 * ;]
1.a setting firmly, supporting.
2.fixedness, firmness, steadfastness: II Pe 3:17.†

στρῆνος.as:
στρῆνος, -ους, τό
(cf. Lat. strenuus), [in LXX: IV Ki 19:28 (שַׁאֲנָן)* ;]
insolent luxury, wantonness: Re 18:3 (a late word, first found in a Comic poet, B.C. 300, v. Kennedy, Sources, 41, cf. στρηνιάω).†

στρηνιάω.der: from a presumed derivative of G4764 (στρῆνος);
στρηνιάω.as:
** στρηνιάω, -ῶ
(< στρῆνος, q.v.), [in Sm.: Is 61:6 (אכל) * ;]
a word which first appears in the middle comedy (Rutherford, NPhr., 475 f.), to run riot, wax wanton: Re 18:7, 9 (cf. κατα-στρηνιάω).†
SYN.: σπαταλάω (q.v.), τρυφάω
